extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and methodological guidance for philosophical inquiry about the data of philosophy: what assumptions may be provisionally accepted, how knowledge/hypotheses are to be justified, and how to distinguish and treat different kinds of mental manifestations (impressions vs ideas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid isolating words/thoughts (beware tacit assumptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not treat a spoken or written word (or the thought symbolized by it) as detachable from the thoughts indicated by other words; avoid assuming that the thought symbolized may be contemplated in isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text warns this misuse leads to radical error: e.g., the sceptical metaphysician who 'will take for granted only this one thing' actually smuggles in many unavowed assumptions (quantity, number, limit, difference, likeness, class, attribute). Insist that every symbol be interpreted in its full meaning, with complementary thoughts, to avoid covertly assuming what the conclusion asserts or denies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisionally accept fundamental intuitions necessary for thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Those conceptions which are vital to thinking and cannot be severed from the rest without 'mental dissolution' must be assumed as true provisionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'fundamental intuitions' essential to the process of thinking are to be accepted temporarily as unquestionable, with their final justification deferred to assessment of the results they produce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify assumptions by congruity with all other dicta of consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: An assumption is justified by showing that all conclusions deducible from it correspond with facts as directly observed — by demonstrating agreement between experiences it leads us to anticipate and actual experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by the gold example: we check anticipated impressions (weight, reaction to nitric acid, malleability, melting point) against observed effects. Repeated agreement between represented and presented impressions is the basis for accepting a hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification as entire congruity between ideal and real presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypotheses (even simple, moment-to-moment recognitions) are verified when there is entire congruity between the states of consciousness constituting them and certain other states given in perception or reflection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truth, for our relative standpoint, is 'perfect agreement, throughout the whole range of our experience, between those representations of things which we distinguish as ideal and those presentations of things which we distinguish as real.' A body of conclusions with no such differences is 'entirely true.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanence/survival of consciousness as warrant for likeness/difference
rubrics_metrics.description: The permanence of a consciousness of likeness or difference (i.e., its survival under critical examination) is the ultimate warrant for asserting the existence of that likeness or difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised judgments arise from more careful comparison; accept the consciousness of likeness/difference which survives critical examination in place of a rash one. 'The permanence of a consciousness of likeness or difference, is our ultimate warrant.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical datum must be a substantive ultimate proposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy requires recognizing some fundamental product of thought (an ultimate proposition) that is co-extensive with all experience and specifies an antithesis between two ultimate classes of experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the unification of knowledge proceeds by arranging smaller classes within larger ones, the ultimate principle that unifies experience must be a statement of likenesses and differences of the most general kind — 'an assertion of some likeness and difference to which all other likenesses and differences are secondary.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify manifestations into vivid (impressions) and faint (ideas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manifesta­tions (what we know) are divisible into two great classes — vivid manifestations (impressions/perceptions) and faint manifestations (ideas/reflections/memories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using terms that import extra hypotheses (e.g., 'sensation', 'state of consciousness'); prefer the neutral labels 'vivid' and 'faint' and attend to the differential characteristics by which they are distinguished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vividness/distinctness as primary discriminator
rubrics_metrics.description: Vivid manifestations are ordinarily far more distinct than faint ones; relative vividness is the conspicuous distinction used to separate impressions from ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although there are exceptional borderline cases (e.g., dim light or faint sounds), the overwhelming mass of experience shows an unmistakable distinction of vividness. When vividness test fails, other means can determine class membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal precedence and dependence (vivid usually precedes faint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vivid manifestations commonly precede corresponding faint manifestations; ideas are generally imperfect, feeble repetitions of prior impressions, and faint manifestations are made possible by the previous occurrence of vivid ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist (e.g., an inventor's conception before the actual machine), but even then the faint conception depends on prior acquaintance with component vivid parts. Cases where faint precede vivid do not mirror the ordinary spontaneous sequence of idea following impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohesion: vivid components cohere more indissolubly than faint components
rubrics_metrics.description: Components of vivid groups are bound together by ties of coexistence and succession and resist detachment; faint manifestations are more loosely aggregated and can be re-arranged or separated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: when looking at a blue vase you cannot separate the vivid blueness from its vivid shape; after closing your eyes you can imagine the shape without the blueness or change the color in imagination. Thus lateral cohesion is stronger in vivid series than in faint series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction pattern: vivid largely unaffected by faint; faint often influenced by vivid
rubrics_metrics.description: The successive faint manifestations (thoughts/ideas) generally fail to modify vivid manifestations; conversely, vivid manifestations frequently perturb and shape the current of faint manifestations (memories, suggestions), though the faint stream can sometimes run independently (reverie, absence of mind).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit peculiar exceptions (to be dealt with elsewhere). Typically, vivid impressions 'drag after them' recognitions and ideas, while the main stream of faint manifestations can continue unrelated to immediate impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of occurrence: antecedents of each order belong mainly to the same order
rubrics_metrics.description: The immediate antecedents to vivid manifestations are themselves vivid; essential antecedents of faint manifestations lie among faint manifestations, though many faint manifestations can be partly caused by vivid ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are important qualifications: bodily actions (muscular tensions) and emotions are vivid yet can be produced by faint manifestations (ideas); and some vivid manifestations (colours, sounds) presuppose bodily conditions that are themselves expressed as vivid manifestations. Recognize such exceptions while maintaining the general rule.
